text:
olivia: FYI i found a pattern where some CI tokens used by 3rd-party integrations lose project attribution after our token-exchange. billing sees the traffic but console shows "unattributed"
kevin: saw that. spike in cost reports tied to "unknown project" label yesterday
sam: quick question: do we have a canonical precedence for attribution? header vs key metadata vs exchange trace?
maria: historically we relied on the API key metadata.owner. the exchange step didn't consistently surface provenance to downstream services
ashley: console UX suffers. customers open tickets: "why is my quota consumed by \"unattributed\"". we should give them a path to claim/migrate keys
lee: proposal for precedence: 1) explicit X-Redwood-Origin header (if present and signed) 2) token-exchange provenance header 3) key metadata.owner 4) historical billing mapping 5) mark unattributed
kevin: + add a confidence enum (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) so billing jobs and alerts can decide whether to auto-assign or require manual claim
olivia: agree. how about we extend token-exchange to emit X-RW-Origin-Provenance: "exchange=project:456;via=sa:789;confidence=LOW"
maria: token-service can add that, but need to ensure we don't leak cross-tenant IDs in headers forwarded to third parties. maybe only emit when destination is internal redwood infra
sam: for auth-proxy we can strip/validate provenance before forwarding. sample config flag: allow_provenance_forward = false|internal_only|all
ashley: UI: show an owner pill with small chevron. if inferred, show reason and confidence. add "claim key" CTA that opens modal to reassign to a project
lee: telemetry: add tags on request: origin_source, origin_value, origin_confidence. emit event `origin_inference` when fallback occurs with field `used_rule`
kevin: rollout plan: step 0 - backfill historical attributions (7d job) step 1 - token-service provenance header (canary) step 2 - auth-proxy tagging (5% canary) step 3 - UI affordance + claim modal step 4 - enable billing reconciliation
olivia: alerting: when unattributed ratio > 0.5% over 15m and total_rps > 500, page eng-platform oncall. also emit ticket to support to batch-notify affected customers
maria: edge-case: exchanges across orgs where exchange.provenance points to origin org A but the final billing project is B. we should keep both tags and surface conflict in UI + add a `conflict` flag in telemetry
sam: dashboard tile: "Auth Attribution: by confidence" with stacked bars (high/med/low/unattributed). table for top 50 keys with `unattributed_count`, `last_seen`, `inferred_project`
ashley: claim modal flow idea: show evidence (header, key.owner, exchange trace), suggested project (highest confidence), allow accept/reject, optionally rotate key on claim
lee: for debug debugging add log output in auth-proxy when debug=true:

{"req_id":"$REQ","origin_choice":"header","origin_value":"project/456","confidence":"LOW","rule":"header_signed"}

kevin: metrics names: rw.auth.origin.confidence_total, rw.auth.origin.unattributed_rate, rw.auth.origin.fallbacks
olivia: small privacy note: when surfacing provenance in UI, strip internal-only identifiers and show truncated IDs or allow admins to hide provenance
maria: i'll send a small PR to token-service to add the provenance header behind a feature flag
sam: i'll make the dashboard once tags are emitted, can start with a grafana panel draft
ashley: i'll prototype the claim modal and copy for error states
olivia: volunteers for RFC review?
kevin: me for billing/telemetry
maria: me for token-service bits
sam: me for dashboards
ashley: me for UI

dev-bot: scheduled: auth-proxy v1.13 canary rollout @ 2024-01-18T14:00Z (5%) :rocket:

olivia: awesome. thanks all. i'll open RFC with the precedence table, telemetry keys, and UX mocks. aiming to ship alpha in two weeks :thumbsup:
